newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns European Union on textile probes.
newsitem.headline: China warns European Union on textile probes.

text.p: China on Thursday called European Union (EU) investigations into Chinese textiles exports discriminatory and hinted at retaliatory action if the probes led to anti-dumping measures.

"...The European Union has taken a series of unreasonable methods and discriminatory policies towards China that are completely intolerable," the International Business Daily quoted a senior textile official as saying.

The EU had failed to show that imports of Chinese textiles had led to a lowering of prices or had harmed Europe's domestic textile industry, it quoted Yu Boge, vice-president of state-run China National Textiles Import and Export Corp, as saying.
The EU has recently stepped up anti-dumping investigations against a number of Chinese products, including major items such as shoes, bags and unbleached cotton cloth.
Yu charged that trade protectionism lay behind the EU probes and that European dyeing and garment firms would suffer if the EU imposed an anti-dumping tax on Chinese textiles.
Yu estimated the tax would cost Chinese textile makers about $100 million a year and cause huge job cuts. He warned of possible retaliatory action from China.
"If they are bent on not changing and insist on having their own way, China will take corresponding retaliatory measures," Yu said without elaborating.
He said the EU was mistaken in treating China as a non-market economy and using statistics from other nations to estimate China's production costs.

Nearly two decades of market-oriented reforms have eroded China's central planning but economists say many of China's state-owned manufacturers are still highly reliant on hidden subsidies such as low-interest loans from state banks.

Chinese exports to the EU totalled $8.7 billion in the first half of 1996, down 0.3 percent compared with the same period the year before. China has said its imports from the EU rose 4.4 percent to $9.0 billion during the period.
In September, Washington announced punitive charges against import quotas for Chinese textile goods, accusing China of using transshipments to avoid U.S. quota restrictions.
China said last Sunday it was temporarily suspending its imports of some U.S. textiles and farm goods in retaliation for the punitive charges.
China said the sanctions were made without consultation and with no clear supporting evidence, adding it had no choice but to impose retaliatory sanctions.
